title: Octoboard control socket: daemon to client
description: One text frame the daemon sends on `/ws/control`. See `apps/daemon/PROTOCOL.md`.

name.description:
Required, and unique within this account's agent compared trimmed and case-insensitively —
the default account's own name takes part in that comparison, which is why it is compared
against [`DEFAULT_ACCOUNT_NAME`] rather than left unchecked. Names are not compared across
agents.

config_dir.description:
Absolute, lexically normalised, exactly as a console's pinned directory is stored today.
Existence is not checked when this is set: the directory is created on first launch (by
Claude Code itself, by the Codex adapter for Codex), so a user pointing an account at a
directory they are about to create should not be stopped — this may therefore name a
directory that does not exist yet.

share_default_config.description:
Whether the account shares what its directory can share with the agent's default account's
directory, by linking each item of `crate::accounts::shared_config::items` into it. The
user's choice, set by `set_account_sharing`; kept local.

share_default_config_incomplete.description:
The last change toward `share_default_config` did not finish: it failed part-way, or the
daemon stopped while it ran (set when a change starts, cleared when one succeeds). Only
asking again for the recorded value or the opposite change clears it; nothing retries it
by itself.

disabled.description:
The user turned the account off for new work: automatic account selection skips it and no
session can be opened on, handed off to or switched to it (`account_disabled`). Sessions
already on it are untouched, and no usage window is started on it automatically. Set by
`set_account_disabled`, until the user turns it back on.

versions.description:
The version of each field a form edits, by path (`crate::state::FieldVersions`): always
every path of the record once a client is sent it, as part of `Settings::accounts`.

Account.description:
A named config directory of one agent, kept once for the whole application and referred to by
id wherever a config directory is referred to — a console's per-agent setting, a session's own
copy of it. Every agent also has a *default* account, which is not a row here: it is the state
of pinning nothing. Its name is [`DEFAULT_ACCOUNT_NAME`] until the user gives it one of their
own (`Settings::default_account_names`, set by `set_default_account_name`), and it cannot be
created or removed.

AccountFallback.description:
An account reference of the document that names no account of its agent on this machine, and
so is bound to that agent's default account.

sessions.description:
The account's sessions working under its directory: in the middle of a turn, with
background work running, waiting for the user's answer (a permission prompt, a question),
holding a message of Octoboard's queued, being written or left unsent in its input box, or
claimed — being started, resumed, switched or handed off, or having their owner changed.

signing_in.description: Whether the account is being signed in.

AccountInUse.description: What runs under an account's directory that a change of its sharing must not move files under.

account.description: The account's id; `None` for the agent's default account.

authorization_url.description:
The page the user authorizes on, once the CLI has given it. Octoboard opens it itself unless
`opened_by_agent`.

device_code.description: The code the user confirms on that page, for a device-code flow (Grok Build).

opened_by_agent.description:
The agent's CLI opens the page in the browser by itself and cannot be stopped from it (Grok
Build), so a client must not open it again, only offer to reopen it.

failure.description:
Why a `failed` login failed, as a coded message of the same shape as an `error`; codes in
`login_failure_code`.

AccountLogin.description: An account's login as the daemon last saw it. Runtime state: never stored.

account.description: The account's id; `None` for the agent's default account.

read_at.description: When the reading was taken, milliseconds since the epoch.

connectors.description:
The connectors the agent's platform hosts for the account (Claude's claude.ai connectors,
Codex's Apps). Empty when `unavailable` is set.

servers.description:
The MCP servers configured for the account, whether by the user or by a plugin. Empty when
`unavailable` is set.

unavailable.description: Why the account could not be read; the two lists are empty then.

AccountMcpInventory.description:
How an agent's account stands with the MCP servers and connectors it has, read through the
agent's own CLI at `read_at`. Runtime state of the daemon: never stored.

AccountName.description:
A reference to an account: its name, which is unique within its agent. The agent is the one
whose entry holds the reference (`accounts.claude` is a Claude Code account), so it is not
repeated here, where a hand-edited document could contradict it. The importing machine rebinds
the reference to the account of that agent and name.

oneOf.description: An account of the agent with the name was there; used as it is.
A resolution said to leave it out.
It could not be created; `error` says why.

account.description: The account's id; `None` for the agent's default account.

fetched_at.description: When the reading was taken, milliseconds since the epoch.

plan.description: The plan as the agent names it (`max`, `plus`, `SuperGrok`), if it says.

email.description:
The email the account is signed in with, if the agent's sign-in record gives one. Read
whether or not the quota could be; `None` for an account that is not signed in or whose
configuration directory is missing.

windows.description:
Empty when the account has never been read. After a failed re-read, the last good windows
stay (with their `fetched_at`) and `unavailable` says why the newer attempt failed.

reset_credits.description:
The account's usable rate limit reset credits (Codex only); absent when it has none or the
agent says nothing of them. Kept, like the windows, over a failed re-read.

AccountQuota.description:
The plan quota of one account as the agent's own CLI last reported it. Runtime state of the
daemon: never stored and never part of an exported configuration.

in_use.description: What refuses a change now; absent when nothing does.

idle_sessions.description:
How many of the account's sessions are idle — at their prompt, waiting for the user's next
message, with nothing left running in the background. They do not refuse a change: it ends
their processes first and resumes them once it has ended. Absent when none is.

progress.description: The change running now; absent when none is.

failure.description:
The last change that failed since the daemon started, until the next one records its
choice.

AccountSharing.description: An owned account's sharing state as the daemon holds it now. Runtime state: never stored.

oneOf.description: It would be created.
An account of the same agent has its name already; it is used as it is and never modified.

The proposed directory is already used by another account of the agent, the default account
included.
The Add account form would refuse its name or directory.

AccountStatus.description: What importing one account of the document would do.

oneOf.description: The directory is there and may be moved to the Trash.
Nothing is at the path: there is nothing to move, and the removal goes ahead without it.

The home directory, the root of a disk or a directory holding Octoboard's data
(`account_directory_protected`).

Something else's directory is, holds or lies inside it (`account_directory_shared`): by
`kind` another account (`name`, `agent`), an agent's default directory (`agent`) or a
project's folder (`name`).

A path that decides it could not be looked at at once (`account_directory_trash_failed`):
the directory, the home directory or Octoboard's data directory, with `cause` `unreadable`
where that is known, or another account's, an agent's default or a project's path, with
`cause` `other_unlooked`.

A look did not answer within the short time the inspection allows: nothing is said against
the directory, and `delete_account` judges it with the full time.

AccountTrashOutcome.description:
What `delete_account` with `trash_directory` would do with an account's config directory, as
`inspect_account_trash` answers.

Agent.description:
A provider's id: the id of one of the registered providers, so it is only ever made from the
registry ([`AgentId::from_wire_name`], deserializing, or a provider's own constant). Ids that
name no registered provider are not `AgentId`s: the wire refuses them and the store keeps them
as text, leaving them out of what it loads.

Serialized as the id string, and generated for the clients as `Agent`, a plain `string`.

default_account_dir.description:
The directory this agent's default account currently resolves to: the directory its own
variable is exported to in the snapshot, else the agent's own usual default. For Grok Build
this is the *source* home a session's per-session home would be built from, never the
per-session home itself. `None` exactly while `availability` is `NotDetermined` — there is
nothing to show yet.

AgentAvailability.description:
One agent's availability and what its default account currently resolves to, derived once per
daemon start from one login-shell snapshot and held as its own derived state on `AppState`
(`crate::agents::availability`) — never as a field of the stored `Settings`, which is written
only by the user's own updates. Travels to a client inside `Event::Snapshot` and
`Event::AgentAvailabilityUpdated`, one entry per agent, always three of them: the
not-yet-determined state is carried by `availability` itself rather than by the entry's absence.

installed_version.description:
The version of the CLI that starts a session now, as `major.minor.patch`; null when the
CLI is not installed or its version could not be told.

latest_version.description:
The latest version published for this install method, as the source names it; null when
there is no source for it (`install_method` `unknown`) or looking it up failed, in which
case `latest_error` says so.

latest_error.description:
Why the lookup of `latest_version` failed, one of `agent_cli_code`'s latest codes; null
when it succeeded or none was made.

latest_detail.description: The English text of the failure behind `latest_error`, when it has one.

checked_at.description: When the check ended, in milliseconds since the epoch.

update.description: The last update of this CLI since the daemon started; null when none ran.

AgentCliStatus.description: One agent's installed CLI as the daemon last checked it. Runtime state: never stored.

started_at.description: When the update started, in milliseconds since the epoch.

finished_at.description: When it ended; null while it runs.

error.description: Why a `failed` update failed, one of `agent_cli_code`'s update codes; null otherwise.

detail.description:
The last line the update printed on stderr (else on stdout), for a `failed` one. English
text of the tool, trimmed and cut to a bounded length.

AgentCliUpdate.description: An update of an agent's CLI as the daemon last saw it. Runtime state: never stored.

id.description:
What Octoboard passes to the agent as its model: an alias Claude Code resolves itself, or
the identifier the Codex or Grok Build catalogue lists.

name.description: The name to show; the catalogue's own where it has one, else `id`.

efforts.description:
The reasoning-effort levels to offer for the model, in the agent's own spelling: the
catalogue's own, in its order, where the model's entry gives them, else the agent's whole
measured set; empty only for a model that takes none. Never unknown. A level the model
does not advertise (the fallback is per agent, not per model) can still be refused by the
agent, or quietly lowered, as Claude Code does with a level its model does not support, so
a listed level is one to offer, not a promise that it is honoured.

version.description:
The concrete version `id` currently stands for, where `id` is an alias (Claude Code's
`opus` standing for "Opus 5.5"); absent where `id` already names the model, or where the
catalogue says nothing about it.

available.description:
Whether the account can use the model: `false` for one the agent would refuse; absent
where that is not known, which a client must not read as either answer.

AgentModel.description: One model an agent offers, as `list_agent_models` reports it.

Availability.description:
Whether an agent's binary resolves on the user's login shell `PATH`, the only test an agent is
held to: whether its config directory holds a login is not Octoboard's business (see
`crate::agents::availability`'s module doc). Three states, not two:
[`NotDetermined`](Availability::NotDetermined) is where every run of the daemon starts, and
only a completed login-shell snapshot ever moves an agent out of it — a snapshot that times out
or fails leaves it there, rather than being read as [`Unavailable`](Availability::Unavailable).

id.description: The agent's id for the task; the same id its completion notification names.

type.description: The agent's name for the kind of task (`type` in its payload), absent when it gave none.

description.description: What the task is, as the agent describes it, absent when it gave none.

BackgroundTask.description:
One piece of work a session's agent left running in the background when its turn ended: a
shell command, a monitor, an MCP call or an agent, as the agent itself lists it.

upstream.description:
For the branch the main working copy has checked out, and no other, the remote-tracking
branch to compare it with: the remote branch it is set to track, else the branch of the
same name on a configured remote (`origin`'s preferred), when the repository has that
reference. A branch whose upstream is another local branch, or whose upstream reference is
gone, is treated as having no upstream; absent when neither exists.

origin.description: The session responsible for the branch, when the daemon can name one; absent otherwise.

BranchInfo.description:
One local branch of a project's repository, as `list_project_branches` lists it: its name below
`refs/heads/`, as a wire path, and the object id its reference named when it was listed — the
commit at its tip, unless the branch is broken (a missing object, or not a commit).

responsible_session.description:
The session working on the branch: the one whose own git reported creating it until the
branch is handed to another. It may name a session that no longer exists.

responsible_title.description: That session's title when it became responsible.

responsible_since.description:
When that session became responsible (milliseconds since the epoch): the branch's creation,
or the transfer.

BranchOriginInfo.description:
The session working on a branch now, with the title that session had when it became
responsible — the record outlives the session, which a project's deletion takes with it.

name.description: The entry's name, as a wire path.

size.description: A regular file's size in bytes; `null` for anything else.

version.description:
A regular file's version, equal to the `version` a live read of it would report while it
stays unchanged; `null` for anything else.

target.description: What a symbolic link resolves to; `null` for anything else.

ignored.description: Whether Git ignores the entry; sent only when true. See `browse::ignored`.

BrowseEntry.description: One entry of a project directory listing.

CalloutTone.description: What a callout says of itself: neutral information, a success, a warning or a danger.

preallocates_session_id.description:
Accepts an id for a new conversation, so Octoboard's session id can be the agent's;
otherwise the agent's id becomes known from its first hook payload.

hook_script.description: Runs its hooks through the per-session hook script rather than an inline command.

status_line.description: Shows a status line Octoboard can feed.

reset_credits.description: Offers credits that reset its usage limits early.

per_session_trust.description:
Keeps the trust its confirmation grants in a per-session home, from where Octoboard carries
it to the user's own configuration.

config_sharing.description: Its accounts can share the default account's configuration.

mcp_inventory.description: Can list an account's MCP servers and platform connectors (`read_account_mcp_inventory`).

Capabilities.description:
What a provider can do that not every provider can, declared so that code and the UI branch
on it rather than on which provider it is.

CellValue.description:
A plain value a report shows: a string, a number or a boolean, as a table cell or a key–value
pair's value holds it.

oneOf.description: `path` is a wire path relative to the project's directory.

A change between two branch tips: never part of a worktree's listing, only of a
comparison's, where the old side is the left tip's and the new side the right tip's.

ChangeEntry.description:
One entry of a change listing: a change between two sides, or a path in conflict, which is
not a two-sided change at all. `stats` is what the change adds and removes, absent where the
daemon does not count it (see "Changes and comparisons" in `apps/daemon/PROTOCOL.md`).

ChangeGroup.description:
Which of a worktree's uncommitted changes an entry is: `HEAD` against the index (`staged`), the
index against the files on disk (`unstaged`), or a file on disk Git does not track and does not
ignore (`untracked`). Part of a change's identity, so one path can be a change in two groups.

oneOf.description: `path` is a wire path relative to the project's directory; `source` the version listed.
No such side: the old side of an addition, the new side of a deletion.

A side outside the project's scope; `repository_path` is a wire path relative to the
repository's root, for display only.

ChangeSide.description:
One side of a change in a change listing. See "Changes and comparisons" in
`apps/daemon/PROTOCOL.md`.

ChoiceOption.description: One option of a choice: the `value` that is submitted, shown as `label` where there is one.

oneOf.description: The CLI's own installer: it updates itself (`<cli> update`).
A package of the npm registry, installed globally.
A Homebrew formula or cask.

None of the above, or one that cannot be told: the version is shown and no update is
offered.

CliInstallMethod.description: How an agent's CLI was installed, which decides the command that updates it.

CliUpdateState.description: Where an update of a CLI is.

ColumnAlign.description: Which side of its cells a table column's values sit on, in the reading direction.

CommitChanges.description:
One commit a branch made since it forked, as `list_project_commits` lists it: its full id, its
first parent's (`None` for a commit with no parent, whose changes are against the empty tree),
its subject line, and its changes against that parent that touch the project, each in the
`committed` group.

empty.description:
The comparison starts from the empty tree: `branch` is empty and `commit` is the empty
tree's id, which is the comparison's `base` too.

ComparisonEndpoint.description:
One end of a branch comparison: the branch, as a wire path, and the full id of the commit it was
resolved to. A comparison reply reports both; a read of one of its changes names both back, with
the comparison's `base`, and the commits alone decide what is read. `remote` says the branch is
a remote-tracking one, named below `refs/remotes/`, rather than a local one.

oneOf.description: Groups components under an optional heading.

GitHub-flavoured Markdown. Raw HTML is shown as plain text, an image shows only from a `data:`
URL and an external link opens in the system browser.

A single-line text field; `pattern` is the source of a JavaScript regular expression the
whole value must match.
A multi-line text field.
A number field.

A date field; `default`, `min` and `max` are `YYYY-MM-DD`. Also a time field (`HH:MM`) and a
date-and-time field (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM`, local, with no zone).

A date field; `default`, `min` and `max` are `YYYY-MM-DD`. Also a time field (`HH:MM`) and a
date-and-time field (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM`, local, with no zone).

A date field; `default`, `min` and `max` are `YYYY-MM-DD`. Also a time field (`HH:MM`) and a
date-and-time field (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM`, local, with no zone).
A single choice shown as radio buttons, one option selected.
A single choice shown as a drop-down.

A multiple choice; the submitted array keeps the options' order. `required` means at least
one is selected.
An on/off switch, submitted as a boolean.
A range slider, submitted as a number.
Submits the form. Named, it adds `name: value` to the submission.

A group of buttons, each of which submits the form with one press and adds `name: <the
pressed option's value>` to the submission.

Lays its children side by side, each child one column; the columns stack where the panel is
narrow.
Tabs, one of which shows at a time. A tab holds no input field and no submitter.
A thin horizontal rule between blocks, with an optional label on it.
A highlighted note in a tone, its `text` Markdown as a Markdown block's.
A list of keys, each with its value.
A figure with its label and an optional change since some earlier figure.
A block of code, highlighted for its `language`, with a button that copies it.
A unified diff, its added and removed lines marked, with a button that copies it.

A block of text with a button that copies exactly that text; monospaced unless `monospace`
is false.

A table of plain values, one cell per column in each row (`null` for an empty one), which
the user can sort by a column and filter unless `sortable` or `filterable` is false.

option.description: The ECharts option, as the schema of the `chart` kind allows it.

height.description: The height of the drawing in pixels; the width is the page's.

summary.description: What the chart shows, in words: its accessible name.

oneOf.description: A chart: an ECharts option within the subset of [`chart`], drawn in the user's appearance.

Component.description:
One component of a page: an object of the kind its `type` names, with that kind's properties
beside it. Every kind takes an optional `visible_when`.

exported_by.description:
The Octoboard version that produced the document, for diagnosing one that misbehaves. An
import never reads it; `null` when the producer did not record one.

settings.description:
The application settings that are not console-scoped. Present when at least one section
of them was exported, whichever consoles the export holds.

accounts.description:
The account structure. Present exactly when the export included it; a reader that does not
know the field ignores it.

consoles.description: The consoles exported, which may be none.

ConflictKind.description: How a path is in conflict, as `git status` tells the stages apart.

default_agent.description: The agent a console session of this console is of.

project_session_agent.description:
The agent a project session falls back to when its project names none; `None` follows
`default_agent`. Read it through [`Console::project_session_default`].

accounts.description:
The account each agent's sessions opened in this console read, by id; one setting per
agent, and a session reads only its own agent's. `null` means that agent's default account
— the state of pinning nothing. What a referenced account resolves to at launch is
`Account.config_dir`, read through `crate::store`, not carried here.

launch.description:
The model and reasoning effort a console session of this console is launched with, in the
agent's own spelling; one pair per agent, and a session reads only its own agent's. `null`
leaves the choice to the agent. Read when a console session is opened or resumed, so one
already running keeps what it started with; a project session never reads it.

project_session_launch.description:
The model and reasoning effort a project session of this console is launched with when
neither the session nor its project names one, in the agent's own spelling; one pair per
agent, as for the console session pair. `null` leaves the choice to the agent. Read at every
launch, so a session already running keeps what it started with.

icon.description:
A custom avatar as an `image/*` `data:` URL of at most 256 KiB; unset shows the default
glyph.

console_session_prompt.description:
The user's own text added after the console session's built-in instructions, inside user
tags; `None` adds nothing. Never reachable through the MCP tools.

versions.description:
The version of each field a form edits, by path (`crate::state::FieldVersions`): always
every path of the record. A write names the version it was based on in `base_versions`.

ConsoleSessionColour.description:
A console session's badge colour, one of a fixed palette of sixteen colour families, in hue
order around the colour wheel and then the muted ones, assigned on creation and changed
afterwards only by the user (see `Session.colour`). The daemon only ever hands the label
around; what each one looks like in the light and the dark appearance is the UI's own
(`packages/ui/src/sessions/sessionColours.ts`), not here. A stored label must stay readable,
so once a release has stored it, one is renamed or removed only together with a schema version
step (`SCHEMA_VERSION` in `apps/daemon/src/store/schema.rs`).

oneOf.description: Valid UTF-8 with no NUL byte; carried in `text`.
Anything else; carried base64-encoded in `data`.

The file on disk; `version` changes whenever its content may have.
`root_id` is the identity of the directory the read was scoped to.
The blob staged in a worktree's index.
The blob in a commit; `branch` is the branch it was resolved from, when it was.

ContentSource.description: What a file body was actually read from, so a reply identifies the content it carries.

oneOf.description: An archived session of the asking project records it: reopening that session continues it.

A session of the asking project that is not archived records it, running or without a
process: its conversation is in use already.
A session outside the asking project, a console session included, records it in any state.

No session records it, and an agent's own records do, in this account (`null` for the
agent's default account).
No session records it and no account of an available, added agent holds it.

ConversationLocation.description: Where a conversation is held, as `locate_conversation_to_resume` reports it.

notes.description: The release's notes as the manifest carries them, Markdown; null when it has none.

holder_floor.description:
The oldest holder version the new daemon adopts the terminals of (`handover_check`'s
`holder_floor`); null when the manifest names none.

channel.description: The channel the manifest was read from.

DaemonUpdateAvailable.description: A release newer than the daemon that the last check found.

oneOf.description: Releases that are not marked as prereleases.
Every release, prereleases included.

DaemonUpdateChannel.description: Which release line the daemon's update check follows (`Settings.daemon_update_channel`).

at.description: When it ended, in milliseconds since the epoch.

error.description: Why a `failed` check failed, `daemon_update_check_failed`; null otherwise.

detail.description: The English text of the failure behind `error`, trimmed and cut to a bounded length.

started_at.description: When it started, in milliseconds since the epoch.

finished_at.description: When it ended; null while it runs.

error.description:
Why a `failed` one failed: `daemon_update_download_failed`, `daemon_update_unverified` or
`daemon_update_replace_failed`; null otherwise.

detail.description: The English text of the failure behind `error`, trimmed and cut to a bounded length.

DaemonUpdateInstall.description:
The download and replacement of the update as the daemon last made one. Runtime state: never
stored.

DaemonUpdateInstallState.description: Where the download and replacement of an update is.

version.description:
Its version; null when the file was replaced by something else (an install script run
meanwhile) and the daemon did not write it, so the version is not known.

holder_floor.description: Its holder floor, null where `version` is.

DaemonUpdateInstalled.description: The release the executable was replaced with.

path.description: The executable that would be replaced, as a path on the daemon's host.

command.description:
The shell command that installs the update over it by hand: the install script, told the
executable's directory and the channel the daemon follows. For `not_writable`, it has to be
run by a user who may write to that directory (its owner).

DaemonUpdateManual.description: An update the daemon found and cannot install itself.

oneOf.description:
The user the daemon runs as may not replace its executable: the directory it lives in is
not writable by them.

DaemonUpdateManualReason.description: Why the daemon does not update itself and the user has to.

oneOf.description: Reading the release manifest.
Downloading the archive, checking it and replacing the executable: `install` says how far.

The executable has been replaced; the update takes effect when the daemon restarts, and no
more checks are made until it has.

DaemonUpdatePhase.description: What the daemon's update is doing. A check and a download never run together.

total.description: The archive's size in bytes, when the server said it.

DaemonUpdateProgress.description: How much of the archive has been downloaded.

available.description: The newer release the last check found and none has replaced yet; null otherwise.

progress.description: How far the archive has come while `phase` is `downloading`; null otherwise.

installed.description: What replaced the executable, once `phase` is `installed`; null otherwise.

last_check.description: The last check that ended since the daemon started; null when none has.

install.description: The last download and replacement since the daemon started; null when none ran.

manual.description: Set while an update is available that the user has to install by hand.

updated_from.description:
The version this daemon replaced when it started, as an update left it; null when it
replaced none. Held until the daemon stops, so a window that opens later is told too.

DaemonUpdateStatus.description:
The daemon's own update as it stands. Runtime state: never stored, and `null` in the snapshot
where the daemon does not update itself (a build without the feature, the desktop
application's daemon, a host it has no release for).

oneOf.description:
Claude Code's own configuration names it (a settings file or `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`): the model
is whatever the user set up, not one Octoboard chose.
Octoboard chose it: the first listed model the account may use.

DefaultModelSource.description: Where the `default_model` of a `list_agent_models` answer came from.

confirms_by_reported_prompt.description:
A write is confirmed only by the agent's report of the prompt it sent, and is marked unsent
when no report comes.

holds_report_for_completion_notice.description: A report is held for the completion notice the agent sends after a turn.

resume_instruction_as_launch_prompt.description:
An instruction for a resumed conversation goes as the launch prompt, which keeps the agent
from showing a resume dialog that would swallow it.

DeliveryQuirks.description: How writing a message into the provider's session differs from the plain case.

DirEntry.description:
One entry of a directory listing. Only directories are ever listed — a project is a directory —
so there is no "is this a directory" field to carry.

oneOf.description: The path the document records.
The last segment of the recorded path, under this machine's default clone directory.
A fresh clone of the recorded remote, into the default clone directory.
A directory the user pointed at.

DirectoryChoiceKind.description:
Which directory a project is placed in. [`DirectoryChoice`] is the caller's pick of one, and
this is the bare name that results report.

DirectoryOffers.description:
The directory each choice would use for a project, present only for the choices its state
allows.

directory.description:
`~/<relative path>` for a directory under the exporting machine's home directory (also `~`
for the home directory itself); otherwise the absolute path. Whatever the export's paths
choice: an account cannot exist without its directory.

DocumentAccount.description:
An account the user owns. Its id, its login, everything the agent keeps in its directory and
whether it shares the agent's default configuration (which moves files outside Octoboard's own
directory, so it is turned on by hand) stay behind.

added_agents.description:
The agents the user has added, in their order. Absent when the exporting machine had not
yet decided the list (it was still finding out which agents are installed), which on import
adds none.

agents.description:
One entry for each agent that has an account of its own, a named default account or a
turned-off default account, in `AgentId::ALL` order.

agent_settings.description:
The settings of the Agent accounts section that are not an account's own. `null` in a
document upgraded from version 1 that had no `settings` region to take them from: importing
it leaves them as they are.

DocumentAccounts.description:
The account structure of this machine, never a credential: which agents the user has added and
each agent's accounts.

accounts.description: The accounts the user owns, in the agent's display order.

agent_tags.description:
The tags the user put on each agent (by wire name), for the agents that have any, removed
agents' included. An agent the document does not list is left as it is on import.

provider_settings.description:
The choices the user made for the settings of each provider (by provider id, then setting
id) that a configuration export carries (`SettingDescriptor::exported`). A setting they
never chose for is not listed, so the importing machine keeps following its own default for
it, and a setting the document does not list is left as it is.

DocumentAgentSettings.description:
The settings of the Agent accounts section that are not an account's own: the three switches,
the tags of each agent and the user's choices for the agents' provider settings. They travel
with the accounts, since they only mean something to the agents and accounts of the machine
they are applied to.

project_session_agent.description: The agent a project session falls back to; absent or `null` follows `default_agent`.

accounts.description: Each agent's account, by name; `null` is that agent's default account.

launch.description: Each agent's model and effort for a console session.

project_session_launch.description: The model and effort a project session falls back to.

console_session_prompt.description: The user's own addition to the console session's instructions; absent is none.

DocumentConsole.description: A console's own settings and the projects associated with it.

name.description: The name the user gave it; `null` when it is unnamed.

position.description: Its place in the display order: how many of the agent's accounts come before it.

disabled.description:
Whether the user turned it off. `null` in a document upgraded from version 1, which did not
carry the flag: importing it leaves this machine's flag as it is.

DocumentDefaultAccount.description:
What the document says of an agent's default account. Its directory is whatever the agent
resolves on the machine, so it is not carried.

description.description: The user's own summary of the project; absent is none.

launch.description: Each agent's model and effort for the project's sessions.

git_workflow.description:
The project's own git workflow settings, each item `null` when it follows the
application-wide value.

DocumentProject.description:
One project's configuration. `path` is an absolute path of the exporting machine, or only the
directory's name when the export left paths out. `remote_url` is what was recorded for the
project, absent for a directory that is not a repository or a repository with no remote, and
also when the export left paths out and the remote is not one that can be cloned from (a local
path would reveal one).

DocumentSessionOrder.description:
The client-held sorting choices of the General section: how sessions and projects are ordered.
Each part is the id of an order, which the daemon neither reads nor checks.

interface_language.description:
The interface language tag (see `Settings.interface_language`): the daemon writes the one it
holds. An import applies it only when this build offers it. Absent when the daemon held
none.

resume_sessions_on_start.description:
Whether the daemon resumes the interrupted sessions when it starts (see
`Settings.resume_sessions_on_start`). Absent in a document from a build that had no such
setting, which an import then leaves as this machine has it.

run_in_background.description:
Whether closing the window leaves the app running in the background, which only the client
holds: the client adds it to a document it saves and applies it from an import's reply, so
the daemon builds none, stores it nowhere and passes it through an import's reply as it
came. Only a client that has the setting (the desktop app) writes it, and only such a
client applies it.

show_menu_bar_icon.description:
Whether the menu bar icon (the notification area icon on Windows) is shown, carried like
`run_in_background`: only a client that has the icon (the desktop app) writes it, and only
such a client applies it.

keep_awake.description:
Whether the daemon holds its host awake (Prevent sleep, see `Settings.keep_awake`). The
daemon builds it when the General section is exported and applies it from an import,
whether or not this host can hold: the value is stored either way.

keep_awake_when.description:
When Prevent sleep holds: `always`, or `working` (while a session is working; see
`Settings.keep_awake_when`). Carried as text so that a name this build does not know is
left out of an import rather than refusing the document.

session_order.description:
How sessions and projects are sorted, carried like `run_in_background`. The client writes all three
parts, so an import sets the sort exactly, and applies each part whose value it knows.

appearance.description:
The window's appearance (`light`, `dark` or `system`), which only the client holds (in its
`localStorage`), carried like `run_in_background`. A value the importing client does not
know is ignored.

markdown_style.description: How a rendered Markdown document is styled (the style's id), carried like `appearance`.

terminal_font_size.description:
The terminals' font size in pixels, carried like `appearance`. The importing client
keeps a value it knows within its own range. A fractional size reads rounded, and anything
that is not a non-negative number is left out rather than refusing the document.

default_clone_dir.description:
The default clone directory as `~/<relative path>` under the exporting machine's home
directory (also `~` for the home directory itself), otherwise the absolute path, whatever
the export's paths choice. An import applies it only when the user asks to, and it must be
usable here (absolute, or starting with `~/`). Absent in a document upgraded from version
1, which did not carry it: importing it leaves this machine's as it is.

git_workflow.description: The application-wide git workflow settings; when present, all of its items are.

keyboard_shortcuts.description:
The keyboard shortcuts the exporting client has changed, by command id, which only the
client reads and writes: the client adds them to a document it saves (an empty object when
it has none changed, which on import means every shortcut at its default) and applies them
from an import. The daemon builds none, stores them nowhere and does not read them, so
they pass through an import's reply as they came. Absent in a document a client saved
without them: importing it leaves the client's shortcuts as they are.

DocumentSettings.description:
The application settings of a document, by Settings section. Every key is optional: a key
(absent or `null`) the document does not carry is left as this machine has it, and a section is
carried when any of its keys is. A field's position sets the key order of an exported file and
of the generated TypeScript, so within its section's group it follows the order of that
section's rows on the Settings page.

oneOf.description: A FIFO, socket or device: listed, never read.

The first frame on every control connection, before the `snapshot`. Its shape is frozen
across generations so that a client of any generation can read it: fields may be added,
never removed or given another meaning.

The answer to `interrupt_session`: whether a running turn was stopped, the session's status
once the interrupt had settled, and what the caller is to know, in prose.

The answer to `set_session_model`: what the change did to the session, and for a restart
whether the relaunch was sent the prompt to carry on with its task.

processes.description: Only for an `inspect_session_branches` that asked for `processes`.

not_stopped.description:
The processes the stop left running, each with the tree it was stopped with, which
`ids` leaves out.

processes.description:
The project's processes, the trees no session owns (left behind in it, or kept under
it), which its removal stops, whether or not the folder goes.

inspection.description:
The token the worktrees it held back are kept under, for `delete_project` to send back
(`crate::branch_cleanup::project`); absent when it held none back.

providers.description: Every registered provider's descriptor data, in the registry's order.

git_statuses.description:
Every git status the daemon currently holds; empty on a fresh start. Carried here, like
the trusted directories, so a reconnecting client never has to ask for it separately.

agent_availability.description:
One entry per registered provider, each starting `not_determined` and
replaced once the daemon's one-time login-shell snapshot lands; see
`crate::agents::availability`.

account_quotas.description:
The plan quota last read for each account of every available agent, the default
account included; empty until the first readings land. Runtime state, not stored.

account_logins.description:
The logins that have started and not ended, whose later updates a reconnecting client
would otherwise have missed; empty when none is running. Runtime state, not stored.

account_sharing.description:
The sharing state of every account the user owns, as `account_sharing` sends it.
Runtime state, not stored.

agent_cli_statuses.description:
The installed CLI of every agent checked since the daemon started
(`check_agent_clis`), the update of one that runs or ran included; empty until the
first check ends. Runtime state, not stored.

daemon_update.description:
The daemon's own update as it stands (`check_daemon_update`, `update_daemon`); null
where this daemon does not update itself. Runtime state, not stored.

home_dir.description:
The daemon host's home directory, so a client can show a path under it as `~/...`; it
is the daemon's home, not the browser's, since the two may be on different machines.
Null when the daemon cannot determine one.

host.description:
The daemon host's own facts: its operating system, how it writes a path, whether it
can make file links, and how its interface names the Trash (`trash`) and its settings
app (`settings`).

keep_awake_held.description:
Whether the daemon is holding its host awake right now (Prevent sleep, see
`crate::keep_awake`): the setting is on, its `keep_awake_when` is met and the host
granted the hold. Runtime state, not stored.

shell_terminals.description:
Every shell terminal the daemon holds, running or exited, oldest first. Runtime state,
not stored.

oneOf.description:
Availability or a default account's resolved directory changed for one or more agents —
the whole three-entry list, like every other upsert. Broadcast when the daemon's one-time
determination lands, and again when an update of an agent's CLI has ended and its entry is
not what it was; nothing else re-determines it during a run.

A plan quota reading finished, or an account's was dropped: the whole list, like every other
upsert.

An account's login started, moved on or ended: its whole state, like every other upsert. The
ones that have not ended are also replayed in a `snapshot`; an ended one is only announced
here.

A check of an agent's installed CLI ended, or an update of it started, moved on or ended:
the agent's whole status, like every other upsert. Every agent's last one is also in a
`snapshot`.

What stands in the way of a change of an account's sharing, the change running and the last
one that failed: the account's whole sharing state, sent whenever any of it changes. Every
owned account's is also in a `snapshot`.

The directories whose projects Octoboard presses every agent's trust confirmation for
changed: the whole list, like every other upsert.

The user settings changed, whole: the single setting today, and whatever is added to
`Settings` later.

Whether the daemon is holding its host awake changed (`keep_awake_held` of the `snapshot`).
It follows the setting, the sessions' work and what the host allows, so it is sent on its
own rather than with the settings.

A shell terminal was created or changed: its title, its state, whether it is busy. The whole
record, like every other upsert.
A shell terminal was closed, or ended with its project or the daemon.

The reply to `create_shell_terminal`, naming the terminal it started. The same record is
broadcast as `shell_terminal_upserted`, which carries no request id.

The reply to `refresh_project_git_status`: the status the check that answers it ended with,
as also broadcast in `project_git_status`, or `None` when that check was abandoned before
it ended (its project removed before it ran or reran, a panic) or had not ended when the
daemon stopped waiting.

A project's `GitStatus` changed, including every transition of `activity` — the animated
icon has something to follow. Nothing is sent when a project is removed; the client drops
its status along with it.

Something about a session the user has to be told, which no status field carries: an
injected capability that will not apply, a setting of theirs Octoboard had to work around.
Broadcast once, when it is found; nothing stores it. `code` and `params` name the notice for
a client to word in its own language; `message` is the English text for a client that does
not know the code.

The `session_notice` with `code` about `session` that was broadcast last no longer holds: a
`message_not_sent` whose message the agent has since reported sending. A client still
showing that notice drops it; one that is not ignores this.

A session of a project the user has not yet agreed Octoboard may press trust confirmations
for — not by its own consent and not through a trusted directory — is sitting at its
agent's folder-trust confirmation; `agent` is the one asking. Broadcast once per
confirmation, and sent again to a client after each `snapshot` while it waits. `trust_dir`
is the directory `confirm_trust` with `trust_parent_dir` would trust, and null when there
is none to offer: it would be the filesystem root, the home directory or one containing it,
the home directory cannot be determined, or the project's path is not absolute.

kind.description:
Whether the session asked for would be a console session or a project session; for
`switch` and `handoff`, which the target is.

console.description:
The console the new session would be in, or the console of the session to bring back,
switch or hand off.

project.description:
The project the new session would be in, or the project of the session to bring back,
switch or hand off; null for a console session.

agent.description:
The agent the new session would run, or the agent of the session to bring back or
switch; for `handoff`, the receiving agent.

target.description:
For `reopen`, `resume`, `switch` and `handoff`: the session an approval brings back,
switches or hands off. Null otherwise.

owner.description:
For `reopen` and `resume`: the session the target reports to, which is where an approval
leaves it; null when it has no owner. Null otherwise.

reopened_owners.description:
For `reopen` and `resume`: the archived owners an approval brings back together with
the target, topmost first, as they stood when the request was made. Empty otherwise.

account.description:
For `resume_record`: the account that holds the conversation's record; for `switch`,
the account the call asked to move the session to; for `handoff`, the account the
receiving session would run on, settled when the call was made. Null for the agent's
default account, and for every other request.

conversation.description: For `resume_record`: the conversation's id as the agent writes it. Null otherwise.

branches.description:
The branches an approval would hand to the new session, as wire paths below
`refs/heads/`: ones the requesting session is responsible for, checked when it asked.
Empty when the request transfers none.

model.description:
For `handoff`: the model and effort the call asked for, as `Session::model` states an
override: absent when the call left it out, null for the agent's own default.

compatibility.description:
For `handoff`: the compatibility switches the call asked the receiving session to hold,
by setting id; empty for every other request and where it asked for none.

requested_at.description: Milliseconds since the epoch, which is what orders several requests oldest first.

oneOf.description:
A session asked with `request_session` for a session that has no owner, or with
`request_resume_session` to resume a conversation, or an owner called `switch_session_account`
or `handoff_session` while the user's approval is required, and its call is waiting for the
user's answer. Broadcast once, when the call is made, and sent again to a client after each
`snapshot`, oldest first, for every request still waiting.
A `session_request` is no longer waiting: every client closes its dialog.

The reply to `open_session`, and to an approving `answer_session_request`: the session that
was opened. For `open_session` it is `starting`, the launch still going on; for an approving
answer the launch has settled and it is running. The same record is broadcast as
`session_upserted` as well, but a broadcast carries no request id, so this is the only way
the client that asked can tell which of the sessions appearing in the tree is the one it
just opened — and therefore the only way it can select it.

directory_exists.description: Whether the local directory exists; absent for a remote repository probe.

oneOf.description:
The reply to `detect_directory_agent` and `probe_git_remote`: the one agent the directory
or remote is set up for, or `null` for none, several, or one known not to be installed.

default_model_source.description: Where `default_model` came from; absent with it.

oneOf.description:
The reply to `list_agent_models`: `agent` and `account` echo the request. `models` is
empty exactly when `unavailable` says why; a client then offers a free-text field or the
agent's own default rather than an error. `default_model` is what a session of the account
gets when no setting names a model (for Claude Code the model its own configuration names,
else the best one the account may use), absent where the agent's own default applies.
The reply to `locate_conversation_to_resume`: where the conversation is held.
The reply to `use_reset_credit`: what the provider did with the request.
The reply to `read_account_mcp_inventory`: what the account's agent reports.

The reply to `sign_in_account_mcp_server` and `sign_out_account_mcp_server`, sent once the
agent's CLI has ended.

The reply to `export_configuration`: the configuration document, which a client saves as
the file the user keeps (see "Configuration export" in `apps/daemon/PROTOCOL.md`).

settings_sections.description:
The sections of Settings the document's settings carry, in Settings order; empty when
it carries no settings.

settings_versions.description:
The version of every settings field as it was read before the current values the
reply shows, for `import_configuration`'s `settings_versions`.

oneOf.description:
The reply to `inspect_configuration` (see "Configuration import" in
`apps/daemon/PROTOCOL.md`): the settings and accounts the document carries,
and one entry per console of the document, in its order.

clone_dir_applied.description:
The default clone directory written, which stays written when the settings as a whole
could not be applied (`settings_error`).

oneOf.description:
The reply to `import_configuration`: what came of the settings and accounts asked for, and
one entry per console of the document, in its order, each naming the console created for
it; no entry at all with `apply_consoles` false.

Where one item of a running `import_configuration` stands, broadcast to every client; a
client keeps the events whose `import_id` is the one it sent. Every item the import will
handle is announced `waiting` first, in the order they are handled, then each moves on to
`creating` (or `cloning`) and ends `done`, `failed` or `not_attempted`; an item left out is
never announced. They are all broadcast before the `configuration_imported` reply is sent
but may reach a client after it, so a client that has the reply ignores later progress for
that `import_id`.

The reply to `list_pages`, oldest first. Pages are not in `snapshot`: a page carries its whole
component tree, and only the session the user is looking at needs its pages, so the
panel asks for them instead — and asks again after every `snapshot`, which is what keeps it
correct across a `page_created` the client was too far behind to receive. A
lagging client is sent a fresh snapshot in place of the events it missed, on the socket it
already has, so nothing else tells it that its list is now short.
A page a session just pushed. The panel showing that session refreshes to it.

A page's form was submitted, or the submission was taken back. `submission` is what it was
submitted with, sent when the daemon accepts it for delivery to the session, before the
message is written; `null` when the delivery certainly failed and the page can be submitted
again. `submission_revision` is the page's revision of it (`Page::submission_revision`):
announcements of one page can arrive out of order, and a client keeps whichever of this and
what it holds has the higher revision, including for a page whose `page_list` it is still
waiting for.

Pages a session withdrew with `delete_pages`, by id. `session_id` names the session that
pushed them. The panel showing that session drops them.
The reply to `probe_path_links`: one entry per asked path, in the order asked.
The reply to `get_project_source`.

root_id.description: The identity of the directory the listing was scoped to.

oneOf.description: The reply to `list_project_dir`. `complete` is false when the listing was cut at a budget.

ignored.description: The `paths` Git ignores, sent only when there are any; see `browse::ignored`.

oneOf.description: Recursive filename matches, possibly cut at a traversal or reply budget.
The reply to `read_project_file`; `project`, `worktree` and `path` echo the request.

The reply to `list_project_changes`. `head` is the commit the staged changes are against,
`null` before the first commit; `complete` is false when the list was cut at a budget.

The reply to `read_project_change`. `head` is the commit a staged change was read against
(`null` before the first commit, and for the other groups); `patch` is the change's unified
patch as `git` writes it, `null` when the reply makes none.

upstreams_complete.description:
Absent when true; false when the upstream lookup was past a budget, so that the main
working copy's branch may lack its `upstream` or `default_branch` though it has one.

default_branch.description:
The remote branch the repository's remote default branch points at, when the main
working copy's branch has no `upstream`; absent when there is none to give.

oneOf.description:
The reply to `list_project_branches`: the repository's local branches in byte order of
their names; `complete` is false when the list was cut at a budget.

The reply to `compare_project_branches`: the two branches with the commits they were
resolved to, the commit they forked at (`base`, their merge base), and the changes from
that commit to the right branch's that touch the project, each in the `committed` group;
`complete` is false when the list was cut at a budget.

The reply to `read_project_comparison_change`: `left`, `right` and `base` echo the request,
and both sides and the patch were read from exactly the base and the right commit.

The reply to `read_project_change_bodies`: both sides with their whole bodies in `file`,
each present or absent, never out of scope.

The reply to `read_project_comparison_change_bodies`: `left`, `right` and `base` echo the
request.

The reply to `list_project_commits`: `base` and `tip` echo the request; `commits` are newest
first. `complete` is false when the changes were cut at a budget, and `commits_complete`
when there were more commits than are listed.

The reply to `read_project_commit_change`: `commit` and `parent` echo the request, and both
sides and the patch were read from exactly the parent (the empty tree for none) and the
commit.
The reply to `read_project_commit_change_bodies`: `commit` and `parent` echo the request.

The reply to `check_daemon_update`: whether it started a check (`started`), and, when it
did, the `last_check.at` of the status as the check started (null for none), so that the
end of this check is the status whose `last_check.at` is another. A check that did not start
changes nothing; `last_check_at` is then null.

The reply to `update_daemon`, once the download has started: the `install.started_at` the
status gives it, by which a client tells this install's end from another's.

The reply to `handover_check`: the running sessions and shell terminals, by id, that the
planned stop would not carry over. `known` is false when the request did not give a floor
and target version that read, so the lists hold everything running rather than a proven
answer. `unreached_shell_terminals` are those of a pending holder that would not be
carried over: not registered with the daemon, their busy state unknown.

media_type.description: The image type the bytes start like (`image/png`, …), a hint only; `null` when none.

FileContent.description: A file body. Exactly one of `text` and `data` is set, by `kind`.

oneOf.description: The agent asks the user each time.
The branch is merged into its target branch locally.
The branch is pushed and a pull request opened.

GitDelivery.description: How finished work leaves its branch.

oneOf.description: Directly on the current branch; the session is given no rule.
On a branch of its own, in the project directory.
On a branch of its own, in a worktree of its own.

GitDevelopment.description: Where a project session is asked to develop.

repository.description: The repository's identity: that of its common git directory.

worktree.description: The worktree holding the project's directory.

scope.description: The project's directory relative to that worktree's root, as a wire path; empty at the root.

repository.description:
`false` when the project's directory is not a git repository; every field below is then at
its empty value.

branch.description:
The branch name; the short commit id when `detached`; `null` when it cannot be read (an
empty repository with no commit yet, or a failed read).

upstream.description:
The configured upstream ref, e.g. `origin/main`; `null` when the branch has none, which is
also when `ahead` and `behind` are meaningless and both `0`.

error.description:
The verbatim, untranslatable `git` or operating-system message from the last failed step,
cleared only by that same step succeeding again — a failed fetch does not stop the local
read, so a status can carry both an error and usable numbers.

error_code.description:
The code of the failure `error` describes where the daemon has one, so a client words it
itself: only `binary_not_found`, for a `git` that cannot be found on the login shell's
`PATH`. Left out for any other failure, and with no `error`.

GitStatus.description:
One project's live git state: its branch and how far it is from its upstream, and whether a
check, a fast-forward pull, or a push is in flight right now. Derived from the project's working
directory on disk, never stored in SQLite; held in memory by `AppState` and (re)built only when
`refresh_git_status` asks for it, with the local branch header also re-read when the project's
refs change — the daemon keeps no timer of its own for this (see `apps/daemon/PROTOCOL.md`'s
"Daemon behaviour, per project").

GitWorkflowOverride.description: A project's own choices; an item left `None` follows the application-wide value.

squash_before_delivery.description:
Whether a branch's commits are squashed into one commit for the feature it delivers, a
separate commit kept only for an unrelated bug fix, before delivering finished work by
merge, push or pull request. Moot while `development` is `InPlace`.

rebase_before_delivery.description:
Whether a branch is rebased onto its target branch before delivery (merge, push or pull
request). Moot while `development` is `InPlace`.

revert_gate.description:
Whether a branch update that quietly undoes changes already on the target branch is
blocked. Independent of `development`.

GitWorkflowSettings.description: The values the git workflow settings take, application-wide or resolved for a project.

turn.description:
The turn it belongs to, counted from 1: a message that opens a turn and the reply to it
share one.

at.description: When the record dated it, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

HistoryMessage.description: One message of a session's history, as `read_session_history` returns it.

oneOf.description: What the user typed.
A message Octoboard wrote into the session: a brief, a report, shared information, a notice.
The agent's final reply to the message of its turn.

HistorySpeaker.description: Who said a message in a session's history.

oneOf.description: Its process runs but the daemon cannot link to it for now, and keeps trying.

HolderLink.description:
How a holder that runs a session's process or a shell terminal's shell stands, when it cannot
be reached.

path_style.description:
How the host writes an absolute path. Paths travel in the host's own spelling; a client
uses this only to split and shorten them for display.

file_links.description:
Whether the host can make the file links configuration sharing needs. When false,
`set_account_sharing` is refused with `sharing_unavailable_on_host`.

trash.description: How the host names its Trash, for wording what a removal does there.

settings.description: The host's system settings app, for wording a setting to change there.

keep_awake.description:
Whether the host can be held awake (Prevent sleep, `Settings.keep_awake`): always on macOS
and Windows, and on Linux only where logind answers on the system bus. When false, the
setting changes nothing there and a client does not offer it.

HostInfo.description:
The daemon host's own facts, which a client takes from the host and never from its own
platform, since the two may be different machines.

HostOsName.description: The operating system of the daemon's host.

HostPathStyle.description: How the daemon's host writes an absolute path.

HostSettingsName.description:
What the daemon's host calls the app its system settings are changed in, for wording a remedy
that has the user change one there.

HostTrashName.description: How the daemon's host names the place a move to the Trash puts things.

ImportFailure.description: Why something was not created or applied: an `error` reply's `code`, `params` and `message`.

oneOf.description: The `account`th account of `agent` in the document, the agent's parts read as one.
The default clone directory, written before anything else is created.
The settings of the Agent accounts section, applied after the accounts.
The application settings, without the default clone directory.

ImportItem.description:
One thing an import creates or applies, named by its place in the document: the indices are
those of `resolutions` and `account_resolutions`.

oneOf.description: Not reached yet.
Being created or applied; for a console, only until it exists.
A project being cloned, which may take minutes.

Created or applied, or an account that existed already and is used as it is. A console is
done once it is created, before its projects are handled.
The same failure the result reports for it.
Its console could not be created, so it was never tried.

ImportItemState.description: Where an item of a running import stands.

oneOf.description: No resolution was given for it.

Its directory could not be obtained, or the association was refused; of a console, that it
could not be created.
Its console could not be created, so it was never tried.

account.description: The id of the account created, or of the one that existed.

agents_added.description: The agents appended to the added agents, in the order they were.

agent_settings_applied.description:
The settings of the Agent accounts section applied to this machine; absent when the document
carries none, or they could not be applied (`agent_settings_error`).

agent_settings_error.description: Why the settings of the Agent accounts section were not applied.

default_name_applied.description: Whether the document's name for the default account was applied.

default_disabled_applied.description:
The flag this machine's default account was changed to, as the document says (`true`
disabled, `false` enabled); `None` when the flag was not changed.

console.description: The id of the console created; absent when it could not be created.

account_fallbacks.description: Empty unless the console was created.

projects.description: All `not_attempted` when the console could not be created.

via.description: How its directory was obtained, for a created project.

project.description: The id of the project created.

account_fallbacks.description: Empty unless the project was created.

directory.description: The directory as the document records it.

foreign_directory.description:
Whether `directory` is absolute in the other operating system's style (a Windows path read
on macOS or Linux, a Unix one read on Windows). It then names nothing on this machine, and
`proposed_directory` is absent; a client can say why.

proposed_directory.description:
The directory as it resolves on this machine (`~/` expanded); absent when the document's
cannot be resolved.

in_use_by.description: The name of the account that uses the proposed directory, for `directory_in_use`.

agents_to_add.description:
The agents of the document not yet on this machine's added agents, which importing would
add, in the document's order.

agent_settings.description: Absent when the document carries no settings of the Agent accounts section.

default_name.description: The name the document gives the agent's default account, when it gives one.

default_name_applies.description:
Whether importing would apply `default_name`: this machine's default account has no name of
its own and the name collides with no account of the agent, those the import creates
included.

default_disabled.description: Whether the document says the default account is turned off; absent when it does not say.

default_disabled_applies.description:
Whether importing would change this machine's default account's flag to `default_disabled`:
the document says and this machine's differs.

provider_settings.description:
The document's choices for the exported provider settings, those this build declares only
(see `DocumentAgentSettings::provider_settings`).

current_provider_settings.description: The values in effect on this machine of the exported provider settings.

InspectedAgentSettings.description:
The settings of the Agent accounts section a document carries, beside the value this machine
has now, so a client can show what applying them would change.

path.description: The path as the document records it.

foreign_path.description:
Whether `path` is absolute in the other operating system's style (a Windows path read on
macOS or Linux, a Unix one read on Windows). Such a path names nothing on this machine, so
no directory is derived from it and `exported_path` and `default_clone_dir` are never offered.

in_document_clone_dir.description:
What the clone-dependent choices (`default_clone_dir`, `clone`) come to under the document's
own default clone directory, which an import takes when it applies the settings and is not
told to keep this machine's. Absent unless the document carries a usable directory that
differs from this machine's; `offers` and `default` are always this machine's.

resume_sessions_on_start.description:
The document's value, or this machine's own when the document carries none, so the line
reads as no change.

keep_awake.description: The document's Prevent sleep, or this machine's own when the document carries none.

keep_awake_when.description:
The document's choice of when it holds, or this machine's own when the document carries
none or names one this build does not know.

foreign_default_clone_dir.description:
Whether the document's default clone directory is absolute in the other operating system's
style (a Windows path read on macOS or Linux, a Unix one read on Windows). It is then the
reason `default_clone_dir` is absent, which a client can say.

InspectedSettings.description:
The application settings a document carries, beside the value this machine has now, so a client
can show what applying them would change. A key the document does not carry is reported as this
machine's value, so its line reads as no change.

oneOf.description: For as long as the setting is on.

While a session is working: starting, working or dormant, or idle with work left running in
the background (any console's, any project's).

KeepAwakeWhen.description: When Prevent sleep holds the daemon's host awake (`Settings.keep_awake`).

compatibility.description:
The compatibility switches (provider settings declaring `compatibility_with`) this level
holds its own value for, by setting id: only the values it holds, so a switch left out
follows the level behind it, down to the agent's value in `Settings::provider_settings`.

Launch.description:
The model and reasoning effort an agent's sessions are launched with, in the agent's own
spelling, and the compatibility switches the level holds. `null` leaves the choice to the
agent.

LineStats.description:
The lines a change adds and removes, as `git diff --numstat` counts them. See "Changes and
comparisons" in `apps/daemon/PROTOCOL.md`.

oneOf.description: The link resolves to nothing.
The link resolves outside the scope, and is never followed.

origin.description: The URL of a remote server; null for a server that is a local command.

plugin.description: The plugin that brings the server; null for one the user configured.

runtime_message.description: Why the server failed, when `runtime` is `failed` and the agent says.

tool_count.description: How many tools the server offers, where the agent reports it.

oauth_sign_in.description:
Whether the account signs in to this server with OAuth through the agent's own login
command, which Octoboard can run (`sign_in_account_mcp_server` and
`sign_out_account_mcp_server`).

LocalMcpServer.description: An MCP server configured for the account.

oneOf.description: The CLI has started and has not yet said where to authorize.

Waiting for the user to authorize in a browser: `authorization_url` and `device_code` say
where and with what.
Signed in, confirmed by the agent itself.
Ended without signing in; `failure` says why.
Ended by `cancel_account_login`.
Ended by the daemon after waiting too long for the authorization.
The account is not signed in to the agent.
The agent's CLI is not installed, or cannot be started.
The CLI did not answer in time.
The agent has no way of listing its MCP servers.
Anything else; `detail` says what.

McpInventoryUnavailable.description:
Why an account's MCP servers and connectors could not be read. The reason is a closed set the
client words itself; `detail` is what the agent or the daemon said, for the cases it helps.

detail.description: What the agent's CLI said, for `failed`; null otherwise.

McpServerAuthOutcome.description: How a sign-in to or sign-out of an MCP server ended (`account_mcp_server_auth_ended`).

oneOf.description: The user ended a sign-in with `cancel_account_mcp_sign_in`, or the account's removal did.
The CLI did not end in time and was killed.
The server takes no sign-in (a local command, a server that has none).
The session had those values already: nothing was written or restarted.
The session had no process: the values were recorded for its next resume.
The session's process was ended and relaunched with the values.

family_version.description:
Whether an id of the form `<prefix><family>-<major>-<minor>[-<patch>...][-<date>]` reads as
"Family major.minor" (`claude-opus-5-5` as "Opus 5.5"), a bracketed suffix kept; any other
id is shown as it is.

id_prefix.description: What such an id starts with, when only ids of one provider's spelling are read that way.

retired.description: Stored spellings that read as no model at all (a retired alias).

ModelDisplay.description: How a model id of the provider is shown.

ModelsUnavailable.description:
Why `list_agent_models` has no list, as a coded message of the same shape as an `error`. It
travels inside a reply because failing to ask the agent must never fail the form that asked.

OffersUnderCloneDir.description:
The offers of a project, and the choice an import would preselect, with the clone-dependent
ones worked out against another default clone directory than this machine's.

submission.description:
What the page's form was submitted with, or `null` while it has not been: set when the
submission is accepted for delivery, before the message is written, and cleared again only
when the delivery certainly failed (`page_submission`).

submission_revision.description:
How many times `submission` has changed: 0 for a page never submitted, raised by one with
each mark and each clearing. A client that hears of the submission twice, from `page_list`
and `page_submission` in either order, keeps the one with the higher revision.

Page.description:
One page a session pushed to its report panel: a console session, or a project session that
faces the user (`show_page`). It belongs to that session, not to its console or project:
`session_id` is the session that pushed it, of either kind. Every page is kept, so the
panel can be paged back through.

PageContent.description: A page: an optional title and the components that make up its body, top to bottom.

view.description:
Where the client reads the file with `read_project_file`, for a file inside the project or
one of its worktrees, or for a directory there, its README or index file when it has one;
absent for anything else. Whether the viewer can show it is for the client to find out by
reading it.

viewer_only.description:
Set for any file in a project, whatever its type, since the system's default application for
a file may run it, and for what the system could launch: the viewer shows it and
`open_path_link` refuses it.

PathLinkKind.description: What a path asked about in `probe_path_links` names.

worktree.description: The worktree it is in; absent for the project's own directory.

path.description: Its wire path below that directory.

PathLinkView.description:
A file in the project, as `read_project_file` names it: the file a path link names, or the one
a directory link shows.

id.description: The agent's own identifier for the connector.

plugins.description: The plugins that bring the connector (Codex); empty for Claude Code.

PlatformConnector.description: A connector the agent's platform hosts for the account.

project_id.description: The project the trees are listed under; absent for a console session.

session_id.description: The console session whose trees these are; absent for a project.

trees.description: How many trees, at least one.

ProcessCount.description:
How many trees there are under one project, or for one console session, in the count of
every project's and console session's trees. It names a project or a console session, never
both.

id.description: The top process, as `<pid>:<start>`: what a stop or a keep names the tree by.

session_id.description:
The session whose launch the tree belongs to; absent for a tree no session owns: one left
behind, or one the user kept.

kept.description: The user kept the tree: no session owns it and nothing stops it unless the user asks.

command.description: The top process's arguments, joined; empty when they cannot be read.

cwd_missing.description: The top process's working directory was removed.

started_at.description: When the top process started, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

memory_bytes.description: The resident memory of every process in the tree, summed.

ports.description: The TCP ports the tree's processes listen on, sorted.

keepable.description: A `keep_processes` naming the tree can keep it; when not, `unkeepable_reason` says why.

ProcessTree.description:
A group of one launch's processes as the user sees it: a top process — one whose parent is not
the same launch's — and its descendants of that launch.

accounts.description:
The account each agent's sessions opened in this project read; one setting per agent, and
a session reads only its own agent's. See [`ProjectAccount`] for the three states.

launch.description:
The model and reasoning effort a session of this project is launched with, in the agent's
own spelling; one pair per agent, and a session reads only its own agent's. `null` leaves
the choice to the agent: there is no console-level fallback, the console's own pairs being
for its console sessions alone. Read when a session is opened or resumed, so one already
running keeps what it started with.

trust_consent.description:
The user has agreed that Octoboard may press an agent's own trust confirmation for this
project's directory without asking, by sending the keystrokes that accept it (see
`crate::session::trust`). The project form of the one auto-trust permission every agent
shares, a trusted directory being the other: recorded once "Trust and continue" in the
dialog the daemon asks with has pressed a confirmation successfully, whichever agent showed
it, and it covers every later session of any agent in the project. It is not the agent's own
trust record, which each agent writes when its confirmation is pressed.

pinned.description:
The user pinned this project to the top of its console's project list. Only the user's
`update_project` changes it.

tags.description:
The user's free-form labels for this project, used to filter the project list. There is no
tag registry: the tags in use are the distinct ones across projects. Stored trimmed,
non-empty and without case-insensitive duplicates, in the order the user gave them.

description.description:
