The user's own summary of what the project is for, read by agent sessions. Stored trimmed;
`None` when blank.

git_workflow.description:
The project's own git workflow settings; an item left `null` follows the application-wide
value in `Settings::git_workflow`.

versions.description:
The version of each field a form edits, by path (`crate::state::FieldVersions`): always
every path of the record. A write names the version it was based on in `base_versions`.

oneOf.description:
Take the console's reference for the agent. What a project that was never given one, and
one whose account was deleted, says.

The agent's default account, even where the console references a named account: pin
nothing, so the agent uses whatever the login shell exports, else its own config
directory.
The account with this id, which belongs to the agent the setting is for.

ProjectAccount.description:
What a project says about one agent's account, which is one more state than a console's
reference has: a console's is an account or the agent's default account, while a project can
also decline to say and leave the choice to its console.

oneOf.description: Take the console's reference for the agent.
The agent's default account, even where the console references a named one.

ProjectAccountRef.description:
A project's choice of account for one agent; `ProjectAccount` with the account named rather
than numbered.

oneOf.description: Clones any git remote, not only GitHub.

resolved_root.description: The directory that path resolves to, symbolic links followed, as a wire path.

root_id.description: The resolved directory's identity; it changes when the directory is replaced.

git.description: The repository holding the project's directory; `null` when it is in none.

git_error.description:
Why the repository could not be read, verbatim, when its directory looks like one but `git`
failed on it; `null` otherwise.

git_error_code.description:
The code of the failure `git_error` describes where the daemon has one, so a client words it
itself: only `binary_not_found`, for a `git` that cannot be found on the login shell's
`PATH`. Left out for any other failure, and with no `git_error`.

ProjectSourceInfo.description:
Where a project's files are read from, as `project_source` reports it. See "Project sources" in
`apps/daemon/PROTOCOL.md`.

label.description: The provider's product name, for a client with no presentation of its own for it.

short_name.description: The shorter form of `label`, where the text around it already says which product is meant.

install_url.description: Where the user is sent to install the provider's CLI.

default_config_dir.description:
The configuration directory the provider uses when none is set, relative to the home
directory (`.claude`).

detection_markers.description:
The names at a project's top level that point at the provider, as `DetectionMarkers` holds
them: its own, then the generic ones it reads. A client shows them to say what detecting
the agent of a repository looks for; several providers may carry the same generic name.

quota_windows.description: How the provider's own interface names its quota windows, which a client's wording follows.

model_display.description: How a model id of the provider is shown.

settings.description:
The settings the user can make for the provider, in the order a client lists them. Their
values in effect are `Settings::provider_settings`.

ProviderInfo.description: One registered provider, as `snapshot` carries it.

QuotaUnavailable.description:
Why an account's quota has no windows, as a coded message of the same shape as an `error`. It
is part of the reading rather than a failure of anything else.

label.description: The model's display name for `weekly_model`; absent for the other kinds.

used_percent.description:
How much of the window is used, normally 0 to 100; a value above 100 is passed on as the
agent gives it.

resets_at.description: When the window resets, in milliseconds since the epoch, if the agent says.

QuotaWindow.description: One window of an account's plan quota.

oneOf.description: The five-hour window.
The weekly window across all models.
A weekly window of one model, named by `label`.
A pool of credits over a billing period.

QuotaWindowKind.description:
The kind of a quota window. Not every provider has every kind: Claude Code has `session`,
`weekly` and `weekly_model`, Codex `session` and `weekly`, Grok Build `credit_period`.

kinds.description: The kinds of window the provider reports at all.

session_window.description: What it calls the five-hour window.

weekly_all_models.description: Whether an account-wide weekly window beside a model's own is named "Weekly · all models".

QuotaWindowNaming.description: How the provider's own interface names its quota windows, which Octoboard's wording follows.

title.description: The backend's name for the credit ("Full reset (Weekly + 5 hr)"), if it gives one.

description.description: The backend's description of the credit, if it gives one.

granted_at.description: When the credit was granted, in milliseconds since the epoch, if the provider says.

expires_at.description: When the credit expires, in milliseconds since the epoch; null for one that never does.

ResetCredit.description:
One of an account's rate limit reset credits that can still be used, as its provider describes
it.

oneOf.description: The credit was used and the windows that could be reset were.

No window of the account is eligible for a reset now. Whether the credit is kept was not
measured.
The account has no credit left to use.
The request's idempotency key had already succeeded.

ResetCreditOutcome.description: What the provider did with a request to use a reset credit (`reset_credit_used`).

available_count.description: How many credits can be used, whatever the list below holds.

credits.description:
The usable credits in the order they would be used: the one that expires first, a credit
with no expiry last. Null when the provider gave only the count, and may be shorter than
`available_count` when the provider caps its list.

ResetCredits.description:
The rate limit reset credits of an account that can be used now. Only present while there is at
least one.

role.description:
Whether the session may own sessions (`Coordinator`) or reports to one and may not
(`Worker`), independent of the parent in `bound_to`: a project coordinator under a console
session keeps the coordinator role, including when it has no children. A console session
and a session with no parent are always coordinators; a session created under a console
session starts as a coordinator and one created under a project coordinator as a worker.
Binding an independent coordinator to a console session keeps it a coordinator, and a
transfer to another console session preserves that; a transfer to a project session makes
it a worker, and a release makes it a coordinator again.

terminal_title.description:
Last title emitted by the terminal, retained when its process ends. The store keeps it as
the agent sent it; the record a client receives carries the session's resolved title
instead, which may come from the agent's records and so be set while no terminal title is.

context.description:
The session's last known context size, retained after archiving. Absent until reported,
and again after a compaction until the next request.

observed_model.description:
The model the agent's records show the session running with, as the agent spells it. Unlike
`model`, which is the launch override, this is what was observed; absent until reported.

observed_effort.description: The reasoning effort the agent's records show the session running with.

default_effort.description:
The reasoning effort the agent runs `observed_model` at by itself, where the records name
that model but no effort and the agent's catalogue gives it a default
(`crate::records::default_effort`). Never stored: it is filled in on the record a client
receives (`AppState::wire_session`), and absent otherwise.

background_tasks.description:
The work the agent has left running in the background while the session is `Idle`: the
session is then waiting for instructions and, at the same time, not finished. Never stored:
it is filled in on the record a client receives (`AppState::wire_session`) from what the
agent's last `Stop` listed, trimmed by completion notifications and cleared by a
`StopFailure`, and is empty for every other status.

switching_account.description:
Whether an account switch (`switch_session_account`) holds the session right now, from the
moment it takes its claim until it lets it go: the process is being ended, the conversation
copied and the process relaunched. Never stored: it is filled in on the record a client
receives (`AppState::wire_session`), and absent otherwise.

paused.description:
Whether the session is at its prompt (`idle`) after a turn that ended abnormally: cancelled
by the user or an owner's interrupt, a declined permission prompt or question that ended
the turn, a usage-limit stop, a failure, or the process ending while the turn was in
progress (the agent `working` or `waiting_user`). It lasts until the session's own status
moves off its prompt (the next turn begins), a turn ends normally, a Claude Code
`SessionStart` begins a fresh conversation, or the agent no longer has the conversation
and the next launch opens a fresh one, and outlives the process: a session resumed
after its process ended mid-turn comes back paused. The store keeps it whatever the
status, as `last_turn_abnormal`; the record a client receives (`AppState::wire_session`)
carries it only while the status shown is `idle`, and is absent otherwise.

prompt_on_launch.description:
Whether a launch of this session that is pending or under way will hand the agent a
prompt, so that it is `working` once it is up. A new open sets it from the first record
that announces the session; a relaunch sets it inside `relaunch_session_with`, once the
refusals are past and it is known the agent is handed a prompt (an instruction, a continue
prompt, or an owed owner notice). It is cleared when the launch's claim is released. Never
stored: it is filled in on the record a client receives (`AppState::wire_session`), and
absent otherwise.

screen_inexact.description:
Whether the screen a client is first painted was rebuilt, after a restart of the daemon
that left the session's process running, from the last of the raw output a holder kept of
it, rather than followed from the start: it may differ from what the agent has on its own
screen until the agent redraws it. It lasts as long as the process does. Never stored: it
is filled in on the record a client receives (`AppState::wire_session`), and absent
otherwise.

holder_link.description:
Whether the holder that runs the session's process can be reached: `pending` while it runs
but cannot be linked to, and absent while it can, or no holder runs the process. While
pending, the process goes on and the session stays claimed: it is neither interrupted nor
resumed, and what is asked of its process fails. Never stored: it is filled in on the
record a client receives (`AppState::wire_session`).

has_conversation.description:
Whether this session has a conversation on the agent's side: a turn taken, or one resumed
at open. Until it has, the agent has stored no conversation to resume: `claude --resume`
on such an id fails outright with "No conversation found", and a session the user opened
and never typed into is the common case of that. A resume therefore starts a fresh
conversation rather than failing.

bound_to.description:
The parent this session reports to, or `None` for an independent session. A parent is a
console session of the same console or a coordinator of the same project. The hierarchy
has at most two reporting edges. Binding and transfer set this id; release clears it.
Console sessions have no parent. Reports route directly by this id, since a console can
have several console sessions. The storage and wire field retain their existing name.

colour.description:
A console session's badge colour, assigned on creation and changed afterwards only by
`set_session_colour` (see `ConsoleSessionColour`). `None` for a project session, which
carries no colour of its own.

ordinal.description:
A console session's place in its console's history, one past the highest ordinal ever
used there. Never reused after archiving or deletion. `None` for a project session.

account_id.description:
The account this session's own agent reads, by id: the one chosen for the session, else the
project's reference for that agent, else the console's, as they stood when the session was
opened. `None` means the default account. Written when the session is opened and by a
successful switch of its account, and by nothing else.

config_dir.description:
The configuration directory of this session's own agent that it launches with:
`account_id`'s directory at the time it was recorded, or unset when it names the default
account. An agent keeps a conversation's transcript under that directory, so a resume finds
it only when relaunched with the same one — which is why this is the session's own copy and
a later edit of the account's directory never reaches a session that already exists.
Written together with `account_id`, never alone.

model.description:
This session's model override: absent inherits its project's (or console's) current
setting, explicit null leaves the choice to the agent, and a value pins the model.

effort.description: The reasoning effort override, with the same inheritance rule as `model`.

compatibility.description:
The compatibility switches (provider settings declaring `compatibility_with`) this session
holds its own value for, by setting id; only what it holds, so one left out follows the
project's, else the console's, else the agent's value, read at every launch like `model`.

pinned.description:
The user pinned this session to the top of its list. Only `set_session_pinned` changes it,
and a pinned session stays pinned across archiving and resuming.

locked.description: Prevents archiving and deletion until the user unlocks the session.

oneOf.description: Whether the worktree is or holds another project's folder could not be told, so it is kept.

The worktree is the home directory, the root of a disk or a directory holding Octoboard's
data, so it is kept.

SessionBranchCause.description: Why a `failed` [`SessionBranchItem`] is left, as a client words it.

repository.description: The repository's canonical common directory, as a wire path.

branch.description:
The branch, as a wire path; for a worktree, the branch it has checked out, `None` for one
with a detached `HEAD`.

path.description: The worktree's canonical root, as a wire path; `None` for a branch.

uncommitted.description:
Whether the worktree has modified or untracked files, whatever its state; false for a
branch, and where it was not read.

tip.description:
The commit a branch points at, as a full object id: what a forced removal is pinned to.
Absent for a worktree, and where it could not be read.

project.description: The project of the session the item was found through.

session.description:
The branch's responsible session; `None` for a worktree a project's removal takes although
no session is bound to it.

cause.description:
Why a `failed` item is left, where a client words that itself; `detail` then says it in
English.

SessionBranchItem.description:
A git branch or a linked worktree bound to a session: a branch whose responsible session it
is, or a linked worktree with such a branch checked out. What `inspect_session_branches`
reports, and what an archive or a deletion leaves behind. A project's removal also takes
worktrees bound to no session (`inspect_project_removal`).

oneOf.description: Goes without asking: a clean, unlocked worktree, or a branch git takes as merged.
A worktree with modified or untracked files.
A worktree with initialized submodules, which git removes only by force.
A branch not merged into its upstream, or into `HEAD` when it has none.
A branch checked out in a worktree that stays.
A locked worktree.
A worktree that is a project's folder, or holds one.

Git refused or failed to remove it, or to say where it stands, a worktree is the home
directory, the root of a disk or a directory holding Octoboard's data, or whether it is or
holds a project's folder could not be told.

SessionBranchState.description:
Where a bound item stands. `uncommitted_changes`, `submodules`, `unmerged` and `locked` are what
a forced removal takes; `checked_out`, `project_folder` and `failed` are left whatever is asked.

window.description: The context-window limit, present only once the agent has given one.

used_percent.description:
The share of the window in use, in whole percent, by the agent's own formula. Present only
together with `window`.

SessionContext.description:
How much the main conversation's latest request carried, as the agent's own session record
shows it: a gauge of whether continuing the session is getting expensive, not a running total.

oneOf.description: Starts a new session that has no owner, from the requester's brief.
Reopens the archived session that holds a conversation.
Resumes the interrupted session that holds a conversation.

Opens a new session, with no owner, on an agent's own record of a conversation that no
session holds.
Moves the session `target`, which the asking session owns, to another account of its agent.

Hands the session `target`, which the asking session owns, off to a new session of another
agent.
Refused by the user, dismissing the dialog included.
Nobody answered within the request's time limit.

The requesting session stopped waiting: its process ended, its call's connection to the
daemon was dropped, or its agent cancelled the call.

Recorded and shown, its agent process still being launched; the status of a session
opened by the `open_session` request until the process is up (one opened for an agent's
`open_session` tool or for an approved session request is recorded the same way, though
its caller is answered only once the launch has settled). No agent has reported anything
yet.

A live session whose screen shows one of Claude Code's views of its background agents, which
holds its messages and takes none: the person is looking at the agents, so it is neither
busy nor waiting for an answer. Computed only in the status a client is shown
(`AppState::shown_status`), over a stored `Working` or `Idle`; never stored.
"session".

SessionWindowName.description: What a provider's own interface calls the five-hour window.

confirm.description:
Whether a client asks the user to confirm before saving this choice. The daemon does not
enforce it.

exported.description:
Whether a configuration export carries the user's explicit choice. A setting whose
enabling itself modifies files outside Octoboard's own directory stays out of one, for the
user to turn on by hand; a setting that only becomes a launch flag travels.

shown_to_agents.description:
Whether the agents' `get_settings` tool returns the value in effect. Agents never write a
provider setting.

compatibility_with.description:
The id of the provider whose configuration this switch makes the provider read, when it is
such a switch. That provider declares itself a compatibility source.

SettingDescriptor.description:
One setting of a provider, declared by its descriptor. The values the user chose are kept
per provider and setting id, never as a field of their own.

oneOf.description: One of the choices; unset leaves configuration and resume behavior to the native agent.
On or off, by the user's choice or else by its default.

SettingValue.description: The value of a provider setting: a switch's on or off, or the chosen choice.

auto_close_idle_shell_terminals.description:
Whether explicitly closing a project Terminal panel closes its idle shell terminals.
Off unless the user turns it on; running programs are kept.

auto_delete_unresumable_archives.description:
Whether the daemon's scan deletes the archived sessions whose conversation is proven gone
(see `coordinator/archive_cleanup.rs`). On unless the user turned it off.

auto_approve_session_requests.description:
Whether a session's `request_session` call is approved without asking the user (see
`session_request`). Off unless the user turned it on; only the user's own client changes it.

auto_approve_resume_requests.description:
Whether a session's `request_resume_session` call is approved without asking the user, as
`auto_approve_session_requests` does for `request_session`, independently of it. Off unless
the user turned it on; only the user's own client changes it.

auto_approve_account_switches.description:
Whether an owner's `switch_session_account` calls run without asking the user, as
`auto_approve_session_requests` does for `request_session`, independently of the other
approvals. Off unless the user turned it on; only the user's own client changes it.

auto_approve_handoffs.description:
Whether an owner's `handoff_session` calls run without asking the user, as
`auto_approve_session_requests` does for `request_session`, independently of the other
approvals. Off unless the user turned it on; only the user's own client changes it.

ask_questions_as_choices.description:
Whether the instructions given to every session at launch ask it to put each question that
needs the user's decision or answer as options to pick from. On unless the user turned it
off. Fixed per session when it starts, so a change reaches only sessions begun afterwards
(a console session's file is rewritten at each launch, so it follows at the next one). Only
the user's own client changes it.

keep_sessions_in_own_project.description:
Whether a project session is kept to its own project: its git is refused a ref update in
the repository of another registered project, and its file-edit tools are refused a path
in one. Off unless the user turned it on. The git check reads it at every ref update, so a
change reaches running sessions at once; the edit check keeps the value a session was
launched with, so a change reaches it only in sessions launched afterwards. Only the
user's own client changes it.

interface_language.description:
The tag of the interface language, one of the tags the interface offers; `null` until a
client reports one. It is the one language every client shows (each keeps a copy only to
render in before it has connected) and the one sessions are told to reply in, so a change
reaches every window. Carried by a configuration export in its General section.

keep_awake.description:
Prevent sleep: whether the daemon holds its host awake (see `crate::keep_awake`), when
`keep_awake_when` says it should. Off unless the user turned it on. It acts only where the
host can be held (`HostInfo::keep_awake`); elsewhere it is stored and does nothing.

keep_awake_when.description: When Prevent sleep holds. `working` unless the user chose `always`.

auto_select_account.description:
Whether a new session whose account was left out runs on the account of its agent whose
weekly quota resets soonest and still has some left. Off unless the user turned it on.
Without a weekly pick, try the inherited account, then the first usable in saved order.
A new session with no named agent or account also tries other installed, added agents in
added order when the preferred agent has no usable account. A resume, switch or handoff
keeps its target agent.

auto_switch_on_usage_limit.description:
Whether Octoboard itself moves a session to another account when its turn stopped on the
account's usage limit (see `crate::coordinator::auto_switch`). Off unless the user turned it
on. Only that: it does not choose a new session's account (`auto_select_account`) or answer
an agent's request for a switch (`auto_approve_account_switches`).

auto_start_quota_windows.description:
Whether the daemon starts an account's usage window that has reset but not begun counting,
by sending one minimal request on that account. Off unless the user turned it on.

resume_sessions_on_start.description:
Whether the daemon, once it has started, resumes the sessions that are interrupted then,
whichever run interrupted them (see `coordinator::resume_on_start`). Off unless the user
turned it on; read at each start.

daemon_update_check.description:
Whether a daemon that updates itself (`snapshot.daemon_update` is not null) checks for a
newer release on its own: once shortly after it starts, every six hours, and at once when
this is turned on or the channel changes. On unless the user turned it off. Off leaves only
the check the user asks for (`check_daemon_update`); nothing is ever downloaded or restarted
on its own either way.

daemon_update_channel.description: The release line the daemon's update check follows. `stable` unless the user chose `beta`.

default_clone_dir.description:
The directory a `git` association clones into when none is named: the one the user set, or
`~/Projects` (expanded) while none is. Always an absolute, lexically normalised path.

accounts.description:
Every account of every agent, application-wide. The default account of each agent is not
among these — it is the state of pinning nothing, not a row (see `Account`).

account_order.description:
The user's order of each agent's accounts, by agent wire name, which clients list them in
and automatic account selection takes them in; null entries represent the default account.
Missing accounts are appended and stale IDs are ignored.

added_agents.description:
The agents the user has added, in the order the user set; a newly added agent goes last. Only these are offered for a
new choice; removing one leaves its accounts here. `null` while the daemon has not yet
decided the list (it waits for the agents' availability), which is not the same as the
empty list of a user who removed them all.

provider_settings.description:
The value in effect of every setting of every provider (see `ProviderInfo::settings`), by
provider id and then setting id: each provider the daemon registers has an entry and each of
its settings a key, and the type is `Partial` only because a client may index it by an id
the daemon does not serve. A switch holds the user's choice, else its default; a choice
holds the user's, else `null`, which follows each account's own configuration. Read when a
session starts, resumes or switches account. The choices of a setting its provider does not
export (`exported` false) are kept local to this machine; an exported one travels with a
configuration export.

agent_tags.description:
The tags the user put on each agent (by wire name), which tell a session choosing an agent
what it is good for. Application-wide, and they apply to every account of the agent. An
agent without tags has no entry. An agent removed from `added_agents` keeps its entry, so
its tags are back when it is added again; a client offers and shows only the added agents'.

default_account_names.description:
The name the user gave an agent's default account, by agent; an agent without an entry shows
the client's own word for it. Not an account row.

disabled_default_accounts.description:
The agents, by wire name, whose default account the user turned off for new work, as
`Account::disabled` does for an account row.

git_workflow.description:
The application-wide git workflow settings; a project may override each item (see
`Project::git_workflow`).

versions.description:
The version of each field a form edits, by path (`crate::state::FieldVersions`): always
every path of the record. A write names the version it was based on in `base_versions`.

Settings.description:
The app-wide user settings the daemon stores, and the account list alongside them: a record
that already grows without a new request shape or a new event for every addition, which is
why the accounts live here rather than in a record of their own.

SettingsSection.description:
A section of Settings whose application settings an export can carry and an import apply on
its own; the Agent accounts section is the accounts region instead.

oneOf.description: Not allowed to change a file or directory, or on a read-only volume.
A file is in use: held by another process, or a database locked by one.
A file or directory is gone.
The volume or a quota is full, or a file too large for it.

Something is in the way or not what it has to be: an entry already there, a link leading
elsewhere, a directory where a file is expected or the other way round.

The agent's default directory is no longer the one the links lead into, or the one sharing
was started into: turning sharing off, then on again, shares the new one.

SharingCause.description:
Why something could not be brought in line, for a client to explain it in plain words; the
failure's `detail` keeps the system's own text.

cause.description:
Why, as a whole: the cause the entries share (`other` when they differ), or why the
change could not start when there are none.

items.description: Each entry not brought in line, as the error's `items`.

SharingFailure.description:
A change of an account's sharing that did not complete, in the form `account_sharing_failed`
gives it.

item.description: An entry of the account's directory, or for a conversation the agent's own id of it.

sessions.description: The Octoboard sessions a conversation belongs to, for a failure about one.

SharingItemFailure.description: An item an operation could not bring in line.

oneOf.description: As it was before the operation.
Renamed to its backup, with nothing linked in its place.

Some of its conversation history moved into the default directory, the rest still in the
account's own directory.
Still a link into the default directory.
Not there at all.

SharingLeft.description: What an item was left as by an operation that could not finish it.

SharingPhase.description:
What a change of an account's sharing is doing, in order: waiting, while another account of
the same agent changes, then ending the account's idle sessions, changing the entries, and
resuming those sessions. `waiting` and `stopping` are left out when there is nothing to wait
for or stop, and `resuming` when nothing was stopped.

share.description: The direction: turning sharing on, or off.

done.description:
The entries processed so far, out of `total`: none before `changing`, all of them once
`resuming`.

item.description:
The entry being processed: an item of the account's directory, or, turning sharing off,
the agent's id of a conversation being taken back. Present only while `changing`, from
the first entry on: absent while the change waits for short CLI reads.

SharingProgress.description: How far a change of an account's sharing has got.

worktree.description:
The worktree of the project's repository it was started in (`worktree` of the browse
requests); null for the project's own directory.

cwd.description:
The directory the shell was started in, with its symbolic links resolved. Where the shell
is now is its own business: a `cd` in it changes nothing here.

title.description:
What a tab shows: the title the shell last set with an OSC 0 or 2 sequence, the shell's
name when it has set none (or set an empty one), or the user's name for it once renamed.

renamed.description: The user renamed it, so the shell's own titles no longer change `title`.

busy.description:
The shell is running something: the terminal's foreground process group is not the
shell's own, or the shell has a child process (a job sent to the background included).
Always false once exited.

created_at.description:
When it was created, in milliseconds since the epoch; a project's terminals are listed in
this order.

screen_inexact.description:
The screen a client is first painted was rebuilt, after a restart of the daemon that left
the shell running, from the last of the raw output a holder kept of it, rather than
followed from the start: it may differ from what the shell has on its own screen until it
redraws it. Absent otherwise; it lasts as long as the terminal does.

holder_link.description:
Whether the holder that runs the shell can be reached: `pending` while it runs but cannot
be linked to, the shell going on unreachable, and absent while it can.

ShellTerminal.description:
A plain shell the daemon runs in a project's directory, beside its agent sessions. Live state
held in memory, not stored in SQLite but for the name the user gave it: the record lasts as
long as the shell, which its holder keeps running across a restart of the daemon.

oneOf.description:
The shell has exited on its own. The record stays, with its output still replayed to a
terminal client that attaches, until a client closes it.

ShellTerminalState.description: Whether a shell terminal's shell is still running.

SideKind.description: What one side of a change is.

oneOf.description:
`file` is the side's body, when the reply carries it: only a file side's, and only when no
patch shows the change's content (a binary change, a side alone).

`lines` is the number of lines the side's stored content holds (its newlines, and one more
when the last line is unterminated), counted of the very blob the patch was made from;
`None` where the daemon read no content for the side.

SideRead.description: One side of a change as `read_project_change` or `read_project_comparison_change` read it.

StatSentiment.description: Whether a stat's change is good news, bad news or neither, shown as its colour.

StatTrend.description: Which way a stat's change went, shown as an arrow.

StatValue.description: A stat's figure: a number, or a string carrying its unit.

SubmittedValue.description:
One value of a [`Submission`]: the text of a text-like field or the pressed button's value, a
number, a toggle, or the chosen values of a multiple choice in the order of its options.

SwitchDefault.description: What a switch is while the user has made no choice for it.

TabPane.description: One tab of a [`TabsLayout`]: its label and what it shows.

oneOf.description:
A process of the tree is attached to its agent's own console, which ends it with the
session whatever keeps it.

UnkeepableReason.description: Why a tree cannot be kept.

tree_id.description: The tree the process was stopped with, as the request named it.

name.description: The process's name; empty when it cannot be read.

UnstoppedProcess.description: A process a `stop_processes` left running: still running once the stop was through with it.

oneOf.description:
The system refused to end it for lack of permission: a process of another user, or one
running with more rights than the daemon.

Anything else: the system refused to end it for another reason, or it outlived being
ended.

UnstoppedReason.description: Why a process is still running after a stop.

UpstreamInfo.description:
A branch's upstream: the remote-tracking branch, as a wire path below `refs/remotes/` (such as
`origin/main`), and the object id its reference names.

VisibleEquals.description: What a [`VisibleWhen`] compares a field's value with.

VisibleWhen.description:
Shows its component only while the input field named `field` holds `equals`: a multiple
choice while its selection contains it, a toggle while it is that boolean.

head.description: The commit checked out; `null` in a repository with no commit yet.

branch.description: The branch checked out, as a wire path; `null` when `HEAD` is detached or unborn.

scope_present.description: Whether the project's scope exists as a directory in this worktree.

scope_cause.description:
Why it does not: `source_unavailable`'s `cause`, or `permission_denied` for a read the system
denied; absent while it does.
